podcasts.name: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: First Documented Musical Netcast (June 24, 1993)
podcast.body: On June 24, 1993, Severe Tire Damage performed a gig on the patio of Xerox's Palo Alto Research Center in California, which was broadcast onto the Internet Multicast Backbone. This landmark event was seen and heard by "proto-internet gigs" as far away as Australia, despite terribly slow video and low-fi audio. "The earliest performance that anyone can document is an event that happened on June 24th, 1993."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts

podcast.title: Opening for The Rolling Stones' Netcast (1994)
podcast.body: In November 1994, Severe Tire Damage strategically played sets before and after The Rolling Stones' 20-minute netcast at the Cotton Bowl, realizing the channel was open. This clever move meant they simultaneously opened for the Stones and had the Stones open for them. "So before and after the stones 20 minute netcast, Severe Tire Damage played sets."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Ongoing History Book of Firsts
